### Subject: Opinion on withholding tax obligations under Section 195 on payment of technical support fees to a US company

---

## 1. Purpose and Basis of this Opinion

This opinion is issued pursuant to our engagement letter dated [●], and is based solely on the facts and representations furnished by the management of Nimbus Technologies Private Limited, and on the relevant provisions of the Income-tax Act, 1961, applicable rules, notifications, circulars, and judicial precedents as they stand on the date hereof. ## 2. Statement of Facts

Nimbus Technologies Private Limited ("the Company") pays an annual technical support fee to Solstice Consulting Inc., a US tax resident, for helpdesk-type software troubleshooting services. Solstice has no permanent establishment in India and has furnished a valid Tax Residency Certificate and Form 10F for the relevant year.

## 3. Issue for Consideration

Whether the payment for technical support services is liable to withholding tax under Section 195, having regard to the 'make available' test under Article 12(4)(b) of the India-US DTAA.

## 4. Relevant Legal Framework

- Section 9(1)(vii) & Explanation 2
- Section 195
- Section 90(2)
- **Treaty provision:** India-USA DTAA, Article 12 (Fees for Included Services)

## 5. Judicial Precedents Considered

- Engineering Analysis Centre of Excellence Pvt Ltd v. CIT, (2021) 432 ITR 471 (SC)
- CIT v. De Beers India Minerals (P) Ltd, (2012) 346 ITR 467 (Kar)

## 6. Analysis

The services in question are routine troubleshooting and do not result in the transfer of any underlying technical knowledge, skill, or process to the Company that it could apply independently in future. Following the Supreme Court's reasoning in Engineering Analysis and the Karnataka High Court's ruling in De Beers, the 'make available' condition under Article 12(4)(b) is not satisfied, and in the absence of a permanent establishment, the payments are not otherwise taxable as business profits under Article 7.

## 7. Conclusion / Opinion

The payments should not be regarded as Fees for Included Services under the Treaty, and the Company should not be required to withhold tax under Section 195, provided a valid TRC, Form 10F, and no-PE declaration are obtained from Solstice annually.

**Confidence level:** More likely than not
